name: ESLint — no-console (logger enforcement)
description: A drop-in ESLint flat-config fragment that bans console.* (no-console) so logging goes through the structured logger instead of console.log technical debt — with the logger transport, server startup, CLI scripts, and config files exempted. Spread it into your eslint.config.mjs.

questions.prompt: no-console severity? (error blocks CI; warn nudges)

checklist: Install ESLint if your project doesn't already have it: npm install -D eslint
Wire the fragment into your eslint.config.mjs AFTER your base config: import { noConsoleConfig } from './eslint.no-console.mjs'; export default [ ...baseConfig, ...noConsoleConfig ];
Route logging through the structured logger (the observability template ships src/infrastructure/logging/logger.ts) — never console.*; console.log carries no level, correlation id, or redaction

Sanctioned console sites are pre-exempted: the logger transport (infrastructure/logging/**), server/startup/**, scripts/**, and *.config.* — add a // eslint-disable-next-line no-console for any other deliberate console use
Run your lint script (e.g. npx eslint .) to surface existing console.* calls to migrate to the logger
Severity is set at install via console_level (error fails CI; warn only nudges) — start with warn on a legacy codebase, then tighten to error
